module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 839

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/839](https://www.erdosproblems.com/839)
- [Er78f] Erdős, P., *Problems in number theory and combinatorics*, Proc. Sixth Manitoba Conf. on
  Numerical Math. (1978), 35-58.
- [Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1992).

See also [Erdős Problem 359](https://www.erdosproblems.com/359) and
[Erdős Problem 867](https://www.erdosproblems.com/867).
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Real Finset
open scoped ENNReal

namespace Erdos839

/-- A sequence $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is "sum-of-consecutive-free" if no term equals
the sum of a contiguous block of earlier terms. That is, for all $i$,
$a_i \neq a_j + a_{j+1} + \cdots + a_k$ for any $j \leq k < i$. -/
def SumOfConsecutiveFree (a : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : ℕ, ∀ j k : ℕ, j ≤ k → k < i →
    a i ≠ ∑ l ∈ Finset.Icc j k, a l

/--
Erdős Problem 839 (Part 1) [Er78f][Er92c]:

Let $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
such that no $a_i$ is the sum of consecutive $a_j$ for $j < i$.
Is it true that $\limsup a_n / n = \infty$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_839.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 1 ≤ a n) → StrictMono a → SumOfConsecutiveFree a →
    atTop.limsup (fun n : ℕ => (a n : ℝ≥0∞) / n) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős Problem 839 (Part 2, stronger) [Er78f][Er92c]:

Let $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
such that no $a_i$ is the sum of consecutive $a_j$ for $j < i$.
Is it true that $\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac{1}{\log x} \sum_{a_n < x} \frac{1}{a_n} = 0$?

This is equivalent to asking whether the range $\{a_1,a_2,\ldots\}$ has logarithmic density zero
(see `Set.HasLogDensity`).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_839.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 1 ≤ a n) → StrictMono a → SumOfConsecutiveFree a →
    Set.HasLogDensity (Set.range a) 0 := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Formalize the additional material on the possible lower limit, reciprocal-sum growth,
-- upper-density constructions, and the links with Erdős Problems 359 and 867.

end Erdos839

findings.description: The module docstring describes [Er92c] as "Erdős, P., *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1992)." This is the wrong paper. The paper in which the problem appears is "Some of my forgotten problems in number theory", Hardy-Ramanujan J. 15 (1992), 34-50. The mathematics is unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: Hardy-Ramanujan J. Vol. 15 (1992) 34-50, P. Erdős, "Some of my forgotten problems in number theory" (https://hrj.episciences.org/125, PDF p. 9 = journal p. 42): "Let again a_1 < a_2 < ... be an infinite sequence of integers and assume that (19) a_r ≠ a_i + a_{i+1} + ... + a_j. In other words no a equals the sum of consecutive a's. Is it then true that the lower density of the a's is 0? Perhaps in fact (19) implies that the logarithmic density of the a's is 0 ... It is easy to construct a sequence satisfying (19) for which ... Σ 1/a_i > c loglog x ... The upper density of a sequence satisfying (19) can be 1/2 but probably it can not be > 1/2." The remarks on erdosproblems.com/839 (loglog x construction, upper density 1/2) match this text exactly. The repo's own files 47.lean, 862.lean and 869.lean cite [Er92c] as "Some of my forgotten problems in number theory. Hardy-Ramanujan J. (1992), 34-50".
findings.suggested_fix: - [Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my forgotten problems in number theory*. Hardy-Ramanujan J. (1992), 34-50.

findings.description: The module docstring identifies [Er78f] as "*Problems in number theory and combinatorics*, Proc. Sixth Manitoba Conf. on Numerical Math. (1978), 35-58." That paper appeared in Congress. Numer. XVIII in 1977, not 1978. I OCR'd all 24 pages (pp. 35-58) and it does not contain this problem: chapter I is about Turán, chapter II covers designs, Mullin's graph problem, aliquot-type iterates, weird numbers and divisor sums, and chapter III covers consecutive-integer questions. erdosproblems.com keys by publication year: the Fifth Manitoba paper (published 1976) is [Er76d] in 364.lean and 933.lean. By that convention the Sixth Manitoba paper would carry a 1977 key. So [Er78f] is probably a different 1978 paper. I could not load erdosproblems.com's bibliography entry for [Er78f] to name the correct paper.
findings.source_evidence: Rényi Institute Erdős archive, https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1977-28.pdf ("PROBLEMS IN NUMBER THEORY AND COMBINATORICS, P. Erdős, To the memory of ... Paul Turán", pages numbered 35-58). The OCR has no passage on sequences with no term equal to a sum of consecutive terms. The index https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html lists this paper as "Congress. Numer. XVIII, pp. 35--58, Utilitas Math., Winnipeg, Man., 1977". An earlier version of the question does appear in [Er77c] (LNM 626, 1977, p. 70): "Let x_1 < x_2 < ... be such that no x_i is the sum of consecutive x_j's. Is it true that the density (lower density) of the x_i's is 0?"
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the [Er78f] entry with the bibliographic data erdosproblems.com gives for [Er78f] (https://www.erdosproblems.com/bibs/Er78f). If that cannot be confirmed, drop the made-up details. [Er77c] (Problems and results on combinatorial number theory III, LNM 626 (1977), 43-72) could also be cited as an earlier source.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses a 0-indexed sequence a : ℕ → ℕ and takes the limsup in ℝ≥0∞ of (a n : ℝ≥0∞)/n. So Lean's ratio at n is the source's a_{n+1}/n, and the n = 0 term is a 0 / 0 = ⊤. The source asks whether limsup a_n/n = ∞ for a 1-indexed real ratio.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The limsup ignores the single n = 0 term. For n ≥ 1, a n/(n+1) ≤ a n/n ≤ 2·a n/(n+1). So the Lean limsup is ⊤ iff for every M, a n/(n+1) > M infinitely often. That is exactly the source's 1-indexed limsup a_m/m = ∞, with a_m = a (m-1). I proved in Lean (scratch3.lean, `part1_equiv`, axioms propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound) that `limsup (fun n => (a n : ℝ≥0∞)/n) atTop = ⊤ ↔ ∀ M : ℝ, ∃ᶠ n in atTop, M < (a n : ℝ)/((n:ℝ)+1)`. It holds for every a : ℕ → ℕ.

reformulations.difference: Lean states `Set.HasLogDensity (Set.range a) 0`: (Σ_{k ≤ n, k ∈ range a} 1/k)/log n → 0 as the natural number n → ∞. The source states lim_{x→∞} (1/log x) Σ_{a_n < x} 1/a_n = 0 with x real and a strict inequality.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any A ⊆ ℕ, let S(x) = Σ_{k∈A, k<x} 1/k and T(n) = Σ_{k∈A, k≤n} 1/k. Then S(x) ≤ T(⌊x⌋) and log⌊x⌋ ≤ log x. Also T(n) ≤ S(n+1) and log(n+1) ≤ 2 log n for n ≥ 2. Everything is nonnegative, so each limit being 0 forces the other to be 0 by squeezing. I proved in Lean (scratch4.lean, `hasLogDensity_zero_iff_real`, standard axioms only) that `A.HasLogDensity 0 ↔ Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => S A x / log x) atTop (𝓝 0)`. With A = range a and a injective (StrictMono), Σ_{k ∈ range a, k < x} 1/k = Σ_{n : a_n < x} 1/a_n; this reindexing step was not formalized.

reformulations.difference: The definition forbids a_i = a_j + … + a_k for all j ≤ k < i. This includes one-term blocks and only looks at earlier terms. The source says 'no a_i is the sum of consecutive a_j for j < i'; [Er92c] says 'no a equals the sum of consecutive a's'. Both mean blocks of two or more terms.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Assume StrictMono and positivity. A one-term block a_j with j < i is < a_i, so forbidding it adds nothing. A block of two or more consecutive terms that reaches an index ≥ i sums to more than a_i. So the definition is equivalent to 'no term equals a sum of two or more consecutive terms anywhere in the sequence'. I proved in Lean (scratch5.lean, `sumOfConsecutiveFree_iff`) that `SumOfConsecutiveFree a ↔ ∀ i j k, j < k → a i ≠ ∑ l ∈ Icc j k, a l` under `∀ n, 1 ≤ a n` and `StrictMono a`.

So I cannot say which 1978 paper the site means. I only established that the paper the file names (Sixth Manitoba Conf., pp. 35-58, published 1977) does not contain the problem.
review.notes: Both theorems state the source's problem faithfully. The hypotheses are 1 ≤ a n, StrictMono a and SumOfConsecutiveFree a, and they are satisfiable: I proved in Lean that powers of 2 satisfy all three, and that the odd numbers fail the condition since 9 = 1+3+5. The answer polarity matches the source's 'Is it true that…' questions and is not negated. The `ℝ≥0∞` limsup avoids the junk value of a real-valued limsup on unbounded sequences. `Set.HasLogDensity` behaves correctly: k = 0 contributes 0⁻¹ = 0, log 0 = log 1 = 0 affects only finitely many terms, and 0 ∉ range a anyway. Part 2 implies Part 1, consistent with the source's 'Or even', because logarithmic density 0 forces lower density 0, i.e. limsup a_n/n = ∞. Both theorems are tagged `research open`; erdosproblems.com (snapshot 2026-07-09, 'no solutions claimed') and the teorth database both list the problem as open. `#check` shows `True ↔ …` only because of the repo's default `answer(sorry)` elaborator setting (alwaysTrue); this is not a defect. [Er77c] (LNM 626, 1977, p. 70), not cited in the file, has the earliest version of the question ('Is it true that the density (lower density) of the x_i's is 0?') and could be added as a reference. The only defects are the two bibliographic entries in the module docstring.
